summary: API gateway thread-pool congestion triggering upstream GPU watchdog timeouts and elevated 5xx rate
description:
Issue summary:
During a high-throughput tenant ramp we observed sustained thread-pool saturation in the API gateway that led to head-of-line blocking and amplified backpressure into the serving runtime. Several upstream runtimes hit GPU watchdog timeouts, causing process restarts and an elevated 5xx error rate across the tenant.

Impact:
- ~18% 5xx error rate observed for ArcSight Analytics traffic between 08:20-09:10 UTC on 2026-03-13.
- Streaming sessions dropped; long-poll endpoints returned 502/504.
- Customer reported failed batch embeddings and timeouts in production.

Environment:
- Prod (us-east primary, failover us-west observed)
- Dedicated cluster for ArcSight (tenant-dedicated-gpu-pool-7)

Timeline (local times UTC):
- 08:17: first signs of increased p99 latency at API gateway (alerts)
- 08:20: thread-pool queue length exceeds 95th percentile; backpressure metrics spike
- 08:24: runtimes begin reporting GPU watchdog timeouts and restart loops
- 08:35: support engaged SRE; temporary ingress throttling applied for tenant
- 08:50: autoscaler started burst workers but warm-up delay and GPU allocation caused cascading retries
- 09:05: mitigation applied (temporary thread-pool sizing increase + tenant throttle) resulting in error rate drop to ~2% by 09:10

Observed metrics and dashboards referenced in investigation: api-gw/thread_queue_length, api-gw/handler_latency_ms, runtime/gpu_watchdog_events, runtime/pid_restarts, autoscaler/scale_events
steps_to_reproduce: Synthetic: Replay tenant traffic at a 3x baseline burst with mixed streaming and embedding requests targeting redwood-v1-large model.
Observe API gateway thread-pool growth and head-of-line blocking on long-running streaming handlers.
When queue > 95th percentile and autoscaler is cold, watch for runtime GPU watchdog timeouts within 30–90 seconds due to scheduling jitter.
Confirm 5xx increase in api gateway and runtime logs during the event window.
logs: [08:25:07] runtime-3 gpu_watchdog: timeout waiting for kernel completion (pid=4321); initiating restart
[08:25:09] runtime-3 exit_code=137 (OOM?) --- note: NVML reports no OOM but watchdog elapsed
[08:27:01] autoscaler event: requested 4 extra workers; scheduling_delay=22s; assigned_gpus=2/4
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: API gateway thread-pool configuration too conservative for mixed streaming+batch bursts; long streaming handlers starve short requests and queue up.
Hypothesis 2: Cold autoscaler warm-up latency combined with GPU allocation jitter causes requests to pile on warm-up runtimes, increasing kernel latency and triggering GPU watchdogs.
Checked NVML and dmesg on restarted runtimes: no consistent GPU OOM, but long kernel stalls observed ~40–120s before watchdog fired.
Confirmed presence of slow downstream storage calls in some embedding requests during spike (see linked trace IDs).
Noted that priority-shedding did not activate for this tenant due to misconfigured tenant-priority policy under mixed connection types (stream+rest).
comments: 2026-03-13 09:00 - Anika Gupta (SRE): Engaged; applying temporary ingress throttle at edge for tenant to reduce new connections. Monitoring error rate and queue length.
2026-03-13 09:06 - Riley Chen (Support): Customer notified of mitigation (temporary throttle); asked to confirm if they see fewer failures. Customer reports partial recovery on their end.

2026-03-13 09:12 - Marco Perez (Runtime Eng): Observed repeated GPU watchdog events on two runtimes; collecting core dumps and NVML timelines. Suspect long kernel stalls rather than memory exhaustion.

2026-03-13 11:40 - Anika Gupta (SRE): Increased API gateway thread-pool max_threads from 50 to 80 for tenant route as intermediate mitigation. Queue length normalized; no further watchdog restarts after change.

2026-03-13 15:02 - Product Ops (internal): Recommended follow-up: tune tenant-priority-shedding policy, add pre-warm step for autoscaler under mixed-workload spikes, and add guardrail to prevent long-stream handlers from saturating shared pools.
2026-03-14 08:20 - Riley Chen (Support): Customer confirmed full recovery and requested post-incident writeup and scheduled 1:1 to discuss SLA credits. Gave timeline and next steps.
resolution:
Mitigated - 2026-03-13: Applied temporary tenant ingress throttle and raised api-gateway thread-pool size for tenant route; autoscaler warm-up recommended changes queued. Root cause appears to be head-of-line blocking in the gateway combined with autoscaler warm-up delay leading to request pile-up and GPU kernel stalls.

Permanent actions (next steps):
- Implement per-route long-handler semaphore to prevent streaming requests from starving short handlers (ENG-12491).
- Add autoscaler pre-warm policy for dedicated tenants with mixed streaming/embedding workloads (OPS-5593).
- Add a runtime guard to more gracefully handle extended kernel stalls and avoid immediate watchdog restarts (RTE-3302).
- Schedule runbook update and customer-facing incident summary.

Follow-ups assigned to SRE and Runtime teams; ETA for rollouts: 2-3 sprints.
follow_up_tasks: ENG-12491: per-route streaming semaphore - assigned to runtime team
OPS-5593: autoscaler pre-warm policy - assigned to infra/autoscaler
RTE-3302: graceful kernel-stall handling - assigned to runtime stability
